input.summary: ADV-8 ad spend (toys; DE 61%, FR 39%) was 511.16 EUR against 13.25 EUR expected over the 6h window (+497.91). The baseline expects about 0 spend from 19:00 to 23:00. Decomposition: higher click volume adds +372.05 EUR (74.8%). All of the click increase comes from more impressions, and CTR is slightly negative. A higher cost per click adds +125.33 EUR (25.2%). CPC sits at a fixed ~2.635 EUR against 0.613 expected, which looks like a set bid level. The surge started at or before 2026-11-25T19:00, the start of the evidence window. The only other toys advertiser, ADV-5, is flat (-0.5 EUR). That rules out Black Friday seasonality and any toys-wide cause. The unplanned search-ranker (DE) and search-ui (FR) releases at 2026-11-27T00:00 came after most of the excess spend, so they are decoys. Data freshness is ok. The Skeptic ruled out innocence: no plan or seasonal pattern explains the spike. The leading explanation is an ADV-8-specific campaign, budget, bid or daypart change. It stays unconfirmed because the only evidence is the metrics themselves. No change-log entry or seller-side fact backs it, and no specialists were available.

The drop is concentrated in the web search channel: search margin was 8.85 against 667.96 expected (delta -659.11, 109% of the entry delta), partly offset by the 'other' channel at +119.78 (ref-6). Within DE, search fell -330.34 (ref-9). FR web and the feed channel returned no rows (actual null) even though FR freshness was reported ok (ref-4, ref-5). Two unplanned releases happened at 2026-11-27T00:00Z: search-ranker v7.2 in DE and search-ui v3.0 in FR (ref-8). They line up with the search and country pattern, but web margin first changed at 2026-11-26T23:00Z, one hour earlier. Web search margin first changed even earlier, at 13:00Z (ref-11, ref-12). So the timing does not support either release as the trigger. The Discovery specialist was unavailable (ref-14), there is no independent engineering or external evidence, and I ran out of steps before the Skeptic review. This is not confirmed.

Is this a short, low-volume overnight dip, or does it continue past 04:00? Only checkout_conversion has been anomalous for two hours in a row (from 02:00).
Did both PSPs see more declines or authentication drop-offs at 02:00–03:00, even though neither posted a status update?
Did the checkout-web release (2026-11-26 10:00) or the app-android release (22:00) affect the payment-method step? Neither had an expected-effect plan.
suggested_actions: Keep watching checkout_to_payment_rate and payment_success_rate hourly through the next few hours. Escalate if the drop continues past 04:00.
Ask the payments team to pull PSP-1 and PSP-2 decline and 3DS reason codes for 02:00–04:00 UTC.
Check payment-step funnel logs for drop-offs at payment-method selection across platforms.
Hold off on rolling back the DE/FR search releases. They line up with only about 12% of the drop.
input.summary: At 03:00 UTC, checkout_conversion was 0.5361 against an expected 0.6926 (delta -0.1565, z -11.3). The data pipeline was complete, so this is not a data problem. No single cause has been found. The drop is broad: all three platforms fell (iOS, web and Android), both countries fell (DE and FR), and payment success fell for both PSPs (PSP-1 and PSP-2). Breaking the metric into its three steps, about 57% of the drop sits in checkout_to_payment_rate, 30% in payment_success_rate and 12% in cart_to_checkout_rate. On their own, though, none of these three steps is outside its normal range (z between -2.2 and -2.8). None of them stayed anomalous for two hours in a row; only checkout_conversion did, starting at 02:00. Client errors were normal. The only unplanned changes were search releases at 00:00 (one in DE, one in FR). Search affects the cart-to-checkout step, which is only about 12% of the drop, so those releases don't explain it. The Skeptic ruled out planned events and seasonality as an explanation.
